bandReport.notes:
Band b1 = pages p00-p07, Q1-Q56 complete, no gaps. Per-page: p00 Q1-6, p01 Q7-12, p02 Q13-18, p03 Q19-26, p04 Q27-34, p05 Q35-42, p06 Q43-49, p07 Q50-56. Printed page numbers advance by two (p00 is printed page 3, p07 is printed page 17), as expected for the bilingual booklet with the Hindi pages dropped.

SEAM: nothing straddles either end. Q1 is the paper's first question and it is a standalone MCQ — THIS PAPER DOES NOT OPEN WITH A DIRECTIONS BLOCK, unlike the 2019-I sitting, whose p00 carries one at the head of each column. Q56's stem and all four options print on p07. p08 (band b2's territory) opens cleanly at Q57 in the left column and Q61 in the right; Q57 is a standalone MCQ and Q61 is a self-contained question carrying its own grouped-frequency table with no Directions block above it, so b2 inherits no set from me and nothing of mine is stranded.

DIRECTIONS SETS - EXACTLY ONE IN THIS BAND, opening and closing inside it, so b2 inherits none. D16-18 (Q16-Q18, the three-newspaper readership table): its 'Consider the following for the next three (03) items :' block sits at the TOP of p02's RIGHT column, above its own three questions, which all sit in that same column on the same page. Q1-Q15 and Q19-Q56 are all standalone.

STRUCTURE, measured on this band rather than assumed from the sibling: questions per page run 6, 6, 6, 8, 8, 8, 7, 7 — a narrower spread (6-8) than 2019-I's 4-7, and the only data-light page (p02, six questions) is the one carrying the Directions table. NO FIGURES ANYWHERE IN THIS BAND: every geometry and elevation item is stated entirely in words (Q23 the circling plane, Q54 the regular hexagon ABCDEF with towers at B and C, Q56 the two parallel streets), and no page carries a diagram, chart or drawn graph. Q31's chart is a printed data TABLE belonging to that single question, not a figure and not a Directions set, so it is transcribed into the stem.

TABLES: two, both GFM pipe tables with separator rows — the newspaper readership table in the D16-18 context, and Q31's speed/time chart in its stem. Q31's table has a BLANK first header cell, as printed.

MISPRINTS: none found. Nothing on p00-p07 required a flag for a printed defect; the two flags in this file are classification notes (Q49, Q56), not misprints.

GLYPHS CHECKED AT ZOOM (6-10x) rather than guessed: Q2's thirteen-factor product and every exponent in it; Q9's four option expressions (the p/q ordering differs between options and is the whole question); Q15's four-level continued fraction; Q21's surd expression; Q28's recurring-decimal overbars, which are the entire content of that question and differ between the four options only in which digits the bar spans (stem 0.53-bar-over-53 plus 0.5-bar-over-3; options 1.0 bar-68, 1.06 bar-8, 1. bar-068, 1.068 no bar); Q30(d)'s twenty-digit non-repeating decimal; Q38's four a/b/c/d arrangements; Q41's nested radical, where the leading 2 is OUTSIDE the radical sign as printed; Q47's option signs; Q50's exponents 2n and 3n; Q56's '30 km/hr', whose zero prints faintly.

DECIMALS: the booklet's raised middle dot is transcribed as a full stop throughout (0.301, 0.477, 7.5, 5.5, 6.5, 1.33, 2.33, 8.17, 25.2 etc.), per the brief.

RUPEES: the booklet prints the rupee glyph in Q35, Q43 and Q45; transcribed as 'Rs.' per the brief.

INVENTED / APPROXIMATE SUBTOPICS - two, both flagged on their questions. Q49 'Inequalities :: Quadratic Inequalities' is invented; the catalog's Inequalities chapter offers only Linear and Absolute-Value, and the shipped corpus has been using 'Linear Inequalities' as a general inequality bucket (2021-2 Q27 is a rational inequality filed there), so the extension pass may prefer to fold this back rather than add a subtopic. Q56 is filed under Trigonometric Ratios and Identities :: Trigonometric Ratios in a Right Triangle as the closest in-catalog fit for a direction/bearing displacement problem; no chapter covers bearings, and the nearest shipped precedent (2025-1 Q38) went to Triangles :: Pythagoras, which does not fit turns of 150 and 60 degrees.

questions.stem: What is the remainder when \((17^{29} + 19^{29})\) is divided by 18 ?

What is the largest value of \(n\) such that \(10^n\) divides the product

\(2^5 \times 3^3 \times 4^8 \times 5^3 \times 6^7 \times 7^6 \times 8^{12} \times 9^9 \times 10^6 \times 15^{12} \times 20^{14} \times 22^{11} \times 25^{15}\) ?

Three cars A, B and C started from a point at 5 p.m., 6 p.m. and 7 p.m. respectively and travelled at uniform speeds of 60 km/hr, 80 km/hr and \(x\) km/hr respectively in the same direction. If all the three met at another point at the same instant during their journey, then what is the value of \(x\) ?

Priya's age was cube of an integral number (different from 1) four years ago and square of an integral number after four years. How long should she wait so that her age becomes square of a number in the previous year and cube of a number in the next year ?
Which of the following statements is not true ?

options.label: A
options.text: The difference of two prime numbers, both greater than 2, is divisible by 2.

options.label: B
options.text: For two different integers m, n and a prime number p, if p divides the product \(m \times n\), then p divides either m or n.

options.label: C
options.text: If a number is of the form \(6n - 1\) (n being a natural number), then it is a prime number.

options.label: D
options.text: There is only one set of three prime numbers such that there is a gap of 2 between two adjacent prime numbers.

flags: Classification is approximate. This is a direction-and-displacement problem: the speeds and times give two leg lengths, and the answer comes from resolving those legs against the given turn angles. No catalog chapter covers direction/bearing problems; the closest shipped precedent (2025-1 Q38, walk East then South) was filed under Triangles :: Pythagoras Theorem and its Converse, but the turns here are 150 and 60 degrees, not right angles.
